sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the transformation of the chassidim's natural powers into G-dly powers is necessary for the drawing down of the innermost aspect of Atik, and explains that any existence separate from G-dliness contradicts the revelation of Atzmus.

translations.translation: And superficially it seems,
that the drawing down of the innermost aspect of Atik is through the self-nullification of Your chassidim,

and that this—that through the drawing down of the innermost aspect of Atik there will be "I will turn [the peoples to a pure language]"—is through the natural powers of the chassidim becoming G-dly powers.
And it needs to be understood,
for superficially,
this—that through the drawing down of the revelation of the innermost aspect of Atik there will be "I will turn [the peoples to a pure language]"—
is not an additional matter beyond the revelation, but is included in the revelation itself,

for since the true essence of His existence, blessed be He, is the existence of all existing things, therefore through the revelation of the innermost aspect of Atik it will be felt in every thing that its existence is G-dliness
(as above in section 11),
and since through the self-nullification of Your chassidim the revelation is drawn down,
why is the transformation of their natural powers also needed?
And it can be said,
that the transformation of the natural powers is also for the sake of drawing down the innermost aspect of Atik.
And the explanation is,
that since the true essence of His existence, blessed be He, is itself the true existence of all existing things,
therefore,
when there is an existence
(in the person)
that is not G-dliness,
it is a contradiction to the revelation of the drawing down of the Awtsmoos
(innermost aspect of Atik),
and through his natural powers becoming G-dly powers
(for it can be said,
that this is brought about through it being felt in him
(at least in a concealed way)
that the true essence of His existence, blessed be He, is itself his existence)
it is the drawing down of the revelation of the innermost aspect of Atik.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the drawing down by "Your chassidim" is through blessing rather than prayer, because prayer implies a separate self, while blessing expresses the G-dliness within, and relates this to Rashbi's bringing rain through Torah discourse without command.

translations.translation: And based on this, we can explain the emphasis of the verse "and Your chassidim will bless You,"
that the drawing down through Your chassidim is not in the manner of prayer but in the manner of blessing,
for in prayer, which is a person's request that they bestow upon him from above,
it is felt that the person praying is not G-dliness,
but in blessing, which is in the manner of command,
his power to command is the G-dliness within him.
And it can be said,
that this is why the descent of rain that was drawn down by Rashbi was not through a command but through the utterance of Torah,
for the matter of command applies specifically when the one being commanded is a separate existence from the commander,
from which it is understood,
that the revealed actions performed through the command of the tzaddikim
(like Rebbe Pinchas ben Yair who commanded the river to split its waters),
that although the will of the tzaddikim is the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, nevertheless they needed to command that it be according to their will,
this is because the world
(in its feeling)
is an existence unto itself.
And based on this it can be said,
that through Rashbi saying a discourse in the innermost aspect of Torah,
the revelation of the Awtsmoos was drawn down,
that the true essence of His existence, blessed be He, is the existence of all existing things,
and therefore through the utterance of the discourse the rain descended by itself,
without a command.
And similarly regarding the drawing down through the blessing of "Your chassidim will bless You,"
they do not need to command that the drawing down occur
(as above in section 4),
for the blessing of "Your chassidim will bless You"
("they will bless You")
is the drawing down of the innermost aspect of Atik into Malchus,
and at this level, command does not apply.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "He redeemed my soul in peace" refers to a redemption of perfect peace where no opposition remains, including even the aspect of "many" (the public domain) being unified, unlike previous redemptions that involved war or only partial refinement.

translations.translation: And this is "He redeemed my soul in peace,"
specifically "in peace,"
meaning that the redemption is in perfect peace and completeness,
so that no opposing element remains at all.
Not like it was at the journeying of the Ark of Moshe, about which it is said "Arise, Hashem, and let Your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate You flee from before You,"
where the refinement was in a manner of war, and therefore the existence of enemies and haters remained, except that they were in a state of being scattered and fleeing,
and also not like it was in the days of Shlomo,
for although the refinement was in a manner of automatic occurrence,
nevertheless only those sparks that had some aspect of light were refined,
for if even the sparks that became darkened could be included in holiness,
and moreover,
that even the created being,
the affected thing itself
(not just the power of the actor within it)
will be in perfect unity,
as it will be in the future.
And this is what is written "for many are with me,"
that even the aspect of "many,"
those who are in the category of the public domain,
as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said
on the verse
"Let us make man" in the plural,
it is written "and whoever wishes to err may err,"
"were with me,"
that they are unified in perfect unity.
And this is that "for many are with me" is a reason given for "He redeemed in peace,"
that the redemption in peace is specifically through this, that even the aspect of "many,"
not only the sparks of holiness, but even those who are in the category of "many,"
were with me.
And in the manner of our Rabbis, of blessed memory,
that even the men of Avshalom prayed for Dovid.
